rules.rule: Check for causes of generalised itchy rash
rules.problem: Type and trigger right; every check_for item traces to a column header. Not checked for: 'itchy, especially at night' (scabies), 'disappear within 24 hours' (urticaria) and the optional insect-bite features; the red box has no criteria of its own (it only links to page 82), so the absence of a priority evaluation is acceptable.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable insect bites (generalised itchy rash)

rules.problem: Requires burrows AND a papule at one of the four sites. The page's header lists 'bumps and burrows' together, so the AND is defensible, but the PPE column says 'If lesions in webspaces, axillae or genitals, also treat for scabies', i.e. the page treats lesions at those sites as sufficient to act on scabies even without burrows; the rule is stricter than the page in that case. Nocturnal itch is not used.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable papular pruritic eruption (generalised itchy rash)
rules.problem: Hyperpigmentation is encoded as a separate AND-ed finding rather than as a quality of the papules (see c008/c031); the structure otherwise follows the page. 'probable' is right ('PPE likely').
Xeroderma lacks the flexural site (c012/c037) but the scaly-skin site findings carry it; 'probable' matches 'Eczema likely'.
Transience ('usually disappear within 24 hours') is not encoded, so persistent sudden-onset wheals also fire the rule. 'probable' matches 'Urticaria likely'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable drug rash (generalised itchy rash)
rules.problem: The 3-month window is measured from now rather than from rash onset (c048), an accepted approximation.

summary: Nothing is invented or in the wrong rule: all 49 claims trace to the page and every SNOMED concept exists; all six 'X likely' diagnoses are correctly 'probable' and the red box carries no criteria beyond a link to page 82. The most consequential imprecision is the PPE rule, which encodes 'hyperpigmented itchy bumps' as a separate 'Hyperpigmentation of skin' finding AND-ed with the papules rather than as a quality of the papules ('Pigmented' qualifier value exists). Lesser gaps: the urticaria wheals lose 'disappear within 24 hours' ('Transitory' qualifier exists), Xeroderma loses the flexural sites, and the scabies rule requires burrows although the PPE column treats lesions in webspaces/axillae/genitals alone as grounds to treat for scabies.
